# Bitfab setup (Amp, Alpha)

Bitfab records real executions of your AI features as traces, then replays those
traces against your current code so you can tell whether a change helped. This
skill runs the setup and maintenance workflows in the terminal through
`bitfab-cli`, with no editor handoff.

## Alpha scope

Amp support is Alpha. This skill covers setup and maintenance. The Bitfab
improvement loop (datasets, graders, experiments, trace labeling) is not
available on Amp yet, because it needs the native plugin. Run it in Claude Code,
Cursor, or Codex for now.

If the user asks for dataset review, experiments, grading, or "improve my pass
rate", say that plainly and point at the other three hosts. Do not improvise a
substitute.

## Before running

Two independent credentials are needed.

1. An Agent SDK credential for the flow itself. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or any
   cloud provider the Claude Agent SDK supports. Without it the command exits
   before doing anything.
2. A Bitfab login, which is separate. The flow opens a browser when it needs
   one and returns to the terminal.

Node 18 or newer.

Check the Agent SDK credential before the first run:

```bash
test -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" && echo "agent credential present" || echo "set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY first"
```

## Running it

Full onboarding, login through instrumentation:

```bash
npx bitfab-cli init --editor amp
```

One mode, when the user already knows what they want:

```bash
npx bitfab-cli setup --v2 <mode>
```

Pass the user's request straight through so the flow does not re-ask:

```bash
npx bitfab-cli setup --v2 instrument --prompt "instrument the checkout agent"
```

## Modes

| Mode | Use when |
|---|---|
| `wizard` | Default. Login, then instrument workflows until the user is done |
| `explain` | "What is Bitfab?" Read-only, no login |
| `login` | Authenticate only |
| `session-logs` | Read or change session log collection |
| `instrument` | Add tracing to a workflow |
| `modify` | Change what an already-traced function captures |
| `inspect` | Diagnose auth, instrumentation, freshness, or traces not arriving |
| `switch-org` | Change the active Bitfab organization |
| `view` | Render one trace function's plan, read-only |
| `replay` | Create or repair the replay registry |
| `db-snapshot` | Replay against database state as of trace time |
| `templates` | Iterate on how spans render |
| `analyze-repo` | Scan the repo and upload draft trace plans, no prompts, no edits |

Print the state graph for any mode without authenticating or starting an agent:

```bash
npx bitfab-cli setup --v2 <mode> --diagram
```

## How to drive it

Run the command in the foreground and let the user answer its questions. The
flow owns every decision point and every approval, including edit previews. Do
not answer on the user's behalf, and do not pre-empt a question by editing files
yourself.

Relay what the command prints. Do not summarize away a diff or a plan it
rendered for review.

If it exits non-zero, show the error and stop. The usual causes are a missing
Agent SDK credential or an expired Bitfab login (rerun with `login`).

**Spell the mode exactly as it appears in the table.** An unrecognized mode does
not error. The CLI falls back to `wizard` and folds the unrecognized token into
the prompt, so a typo silently runs full onboarding instead of the one mode the
user asked for. If the flow starts a wizard when the user asked for something
narrower, that is the likely cause. Stop and re-run with the correct mode.
